Demo 2: single dot (0) at row2,col1, below line at bottom row9? Line is the last row (row 9). Output: dot stays; a vertical bar of color 0 painted rows 3-8 at col 1 (above dot, going to grid edge/line); and on line row 9: cells col0=9, col1=0(dot), cols2-5=9.

So rule refined: dots lie adjacent to a line; the bar extends from dot AWAY from line until grid edge, in the dot's column? Demo1: dots were BELOW the line (line row4, dots rows6,7,8)? Actually demo1 line at row4, dots at rows 6-8 → bars extended UP toward line? Painted rows 3&5 — hmm no, vertical was up to row3 which is above line. Wait line row4, painted rows 3..5 col dotcol... dots rows6,7,8. Bar from dot upward covering rows between line and dot inclusive: rows 3..6 for dot6? painted rows 3,4(kept as 9 because line),5,6 ✓ plus dot rows. Yes! Vertical line through dot from line down to dot. And horizontal bar at rows adjacent to line (3,5) spanning cluster anchor c-1..c+4.

Demo2: dot above line(row9): vertical up from dot to grid edge rows 2..8 (col1), dot at row2 topmost so full span. Horizontal: none visible except line itself? Output row9: 909999 — line colored 9 with dot 0 kept. In demo1 the line stayed 9 too (rows1,4 unchanged, though dot colors overlap?). Demo1 line rows unchanged. OK.

So rule: dots emit ray TOWARD the line (perpendicular?), painting cells until hitting line or edge; plus horizontal bar on both sides of line spanning [dotcol-1, dotcol+4] clipped, using LEFTMOST dot of each column-cluster? In demo1 two lines (rows 1 & 4): bars only at rows 3&5 = adjacent to line4 (the relevant one where dots are relative). Hmm demo1 has line at row1 and row4; dots below row4. Bars at rows adjacent to row4 only. Test has single line row10, dots both sides: bars at rows 9 and 11.

Cluster anchoring confusion: maybe simpler: per dot, horizontal bar spans [dotcol-1, dotcol+4] but merged per cluster defined by gap≤3, anchored at leftmost dot's extent. But actually alternative: each dot paints its own [c-1,c+4]; merging is union. That gave demo conflict. Unless bars clip at other bars... Let me recheck demo1 painted: rows 3&5, cols 5..10 and 15..17. Dot cols 6,9,16. If each dot independently [c-1,c+4]: 5..10, 8..13, 15..17. Union would include 11,12,13. Not present. So definitely merged. With merge distance ≤3 among dots sharing... Actually maybe the rule: dots within distance 4 in the same column form ONE horizontal segment, and that segment's columns span min(c)-1 .. max(c)+4, then clipped?? {6,9}: max+4=13 → 5..13 ✗.

Hmm, what if the horizontal segment length is fixed 6, anchored at the LEFTMOST dot minus1? {6,9}→5..10 ✓. {16}→15..17 ✓. For test below-line dots cols 0,7,11,13: groups? distances: 13-7=6 (>3 separate), 13-11=2 together, 7-11=4 apart. Groups {0},{7},{11,13}. Anchors: 0→cols max(0,-1)=0..4; 7→6..11; {11,13}→10..17. Hmm but wait, does merging even apply—maybe instead the correct unified rule: every dot paints rows line±1 across [c-1, c+4], AND additionally rays from dot perpendicular to line toward grid edge in the dot's row/column. But then dots 6&9 would both paint up to line anyway... The demo1 painted row3 cols 5..10 AND 15..17 — consistent with union with overlap removed? No—union wouldn't remove 11,12,13.

Let me reconsider: maybe the segment isn't [c-1,c+4] but rather determined differently. Check test geometry another way: maybe horizontal bar anchors extend from dot outward until hitting ANOTHER bar? Or the actual shape: think of demo1 output again, picture it:
```
.....
999999999999999999
.....
.....999999....999
999999699699999969
.....999999....999
......6..6......6.
.........6......6.
................6.
```
Verticals: col6 rows3-6 (dot row6), col9 rows3-8? painted col9 rows 3,4(9-line),5,6(dots),7. So col9 vertical spans 3..8 = all dots in that column! And col16 rows 3..8. So vertical = from line-adjacent (row3, i.e., line_row-1) down to max dot row in that column? col6 max row=6 ✓; col9: rows 3..8, max dot row=8 ✓; col16: 3..8 ✓. So vertical bars cover FULL span between line and farthest dot in column — i.e., the whole column strip from line to bottom-most dot, painted where background.

Horizontal bars: rows 3&5 (line±1), segments 5..10 and 15..17. Dot cols 6,9,16. Span = ? Maybe span = [minCol-1, maxCol+? ] no. Alternatively: the horizontal bar covers columns from first dot-1 to ... hmm 5..10 vs 15..17. 5..10 contains dots 6,9. 15..17 contains dot 16. Segment length: dot 16 bar len 3, others len 6. Difference: dot16 isolated. Length maybe = (distance to next dot)? dist(6,9)=3 → end at 6+3+1=10 ✓ (bar reaches up to just before next dot-1). dot9 dist to next (16)=7 → would reach 9+7=16? but capped/merged into 5..10 region? Overlap: dot9's bar [8,15]? conflicts... 

Simplest robust hypothesis for prediction: use "cluster" idea: connect dots whose columns differ by ≤3; each cluster gives bar [minC-1, maxC+1]? {6,9}: 5..10 ✓! {16}: 15..17 ✓!! Test below-line clusters: {0},{7},{11,13}: {11,13}→10..14?? wait maxC+1=14, but expected 17. Hmm inconsistent with demo? {16} alone → 15..17 matches maxC+1=17 ✓ (len 3 because width allows). For {7}: 6..8. {0}: -1..1 → 0..1.

But is +1 or +4 right? Demo: {6,9} maxC+1=10 ✓ (with +4 it'd be 13 ✗). Isolated {16}: +1=17 ✓ (+4 also 17 here due to clipping W=18 → max index 17; c+4=20 clipped to 17, indistinguishable!). Clipping hides the true extent! Test W=19, dot13 with +1 → 14, +4 → 17 distinguishable. Ugh.

Need a third demo or decide. Given clustering threshold ≤3 and bar extent: let me think of physical intuition: dots represent sensors emitting beams perpendicular and parallel to line until obstacles. Parallel beam along row: travels until hitting edge OR until reaching another beam path? Beam from dot6 goes right: passes col7,8,9(dot column!) — hit dot9's column → stop? Then bar from dot6 covers cols 5..9(+1?) hmm painted 5..10 includes 10.

Alternatively beam from dot6 goes right, dot9's beam goes left; they meet mid → union 5..13? still ✗.

Try: beam stops AT the other dot's column boundary, i.e., paints up to (next dot col)-1 exclusive... dot6: next dot col 9 → cols 5..8 (+clipped start 5)? painted 5..10 ✗.

OK maybe: beam from dot6 rightward, beam from dot9 leftward; they meet; total covered = 5..10 means meeting point 10. Dot positions 6 and 9: 6→right half 5-10? midpoint-ish. Honestly with limited data, the most defensible: cluster dots within distance ≤3; each cluster paints ONE bar on rows line±1 spanning [minC-1, maxC+1]... test {11,13}→10..14 seems short vs intuitive 10..17. Risky.

Alternative interpretation matching both demos exactly: bar from cluster spans [minC-1, maxC+1] — check demo2: single dot at col1, line above it. Bars rows 8 and... demo2 line is bottom (row9), bar rows should be 8 and 10(clipped) — row10 doesn't exist. Horizontal bar visible? Output row9 shows only the line colored. Where's the bar on row8? Not painted! So demo2 has NO horizontal bar? Only the vertical ray. Interesting — so horizontal bars only appear when there are multiple dots/clusters? In demo1, clusters: {6,9}, {16} → bars appeared. In demo2, single dot → no bar?

Maybe horizontal bars come in PAIRS symmetric about line only when...? Or maybe horizontal bar exists but overlaps nothing and demo2 bar at row8 would be row8: cells col0..2 = 9? Output row8 = "999333"! YES — row8 painted cols0,1,2 = 9. I misread earlier. Row8: 9 9 9 3 3 3. So bar on row8 (line-1) spans cols 0..2 = minC-1=-1→0 .. maxC+1=2 ✓!!! And row9 (line itself) recolored: cell0=9, col1=dot0, rest 9?? Why cells 2-5 become 9 on the line? Hmm — on the line row, everything gets colored 9 except dots (col1 stays 0). Weird but maybe: the line recolors because... the bar under the line? Like the ray continues THROUGH and beyond? Ray from dot downward hits line and continues painting the line cells after the dot: cols 2..5 = 9, and before dot col0=9. Everything non-dot on the line becomes 9. And bar rows line±1 spanning [c-1,c+1].

Check demo1 with this: line rows 1 and 4. Dots below line4. Rays go DOWN? Dots already below line. Hmm, vertical in demo1 went UP from dot to line. Direction: away from... dot emits ray toward nearest line, stopping at line, then continuing THROUGH the line painting its cells beyond. Demo2: dot above line9 → ray down: rows3..8 col1 ✓, passes through line row9, continues cols2..5 ✓, and also col0=9 (before dot on line, since dot at col1, ray spans whole line except dot). ✓✓✓
Demo1: dot(6,6), line row4 above: ray up: rows5..3 col6 ✓, pass line row4, continue rows1..0? painted rows 3..6 only — not beyond line1. Because line1 at row1 is boundary and row0 painted all 5 (unchanged). Hmm contradiction: ray shouldn't stop at line1 unless rays only travel until first line encountered? First line from dot(6,6) upward is row4 ✓ stops there. But then why does demo2 ray continue past line9 (bottom edge) — because no other line above? In demo2, line9 IS the bottom edge; ray stops at grid edge. Consistent! Ray: from dot toward the closest line, passes through it, continues to grid edge — but stops at the NEXT line. Demo1: next line above row4 is row1; ray should continue rows0..2 — but output rows0,2 col6 are 5. ✗.

Unless ray only goes ONE step past the line: paints line cell, then stops. Demo1: rows 3..5 painted + line4 = dot up to line + immediate continuation... but then demo2 line9: only cell col0=9 (immediate continuation is row9 which IS the line) ✓ both sides col0 and cols2..5? Cols 2..5 are beyond dot — those would need the ray to spread horizontally after passing the line? Hmm like the ray bends: enters line perpendicularly and continues along the line?

New idea: the shape drawn = a "T"/crossbar pattern centered on the dot-column: ray from dot toward line, plus the line row recolored fully, plus bars on lines±1 over [c-1,c+1]... demo1 contradicts (lines are rows1,4 and bars at 3,5 only — bar at row2/0 missing). So ray from dot toward line4 only ✓, doesn't reach line1. But then why would ray pass line4 entirely in demo2 to repaint the whole line row? Maybe rule: repaint the ENTIRE line crossing (all its cells, keeping dots) when the dot lies directly adjacent/in alignment? Both demo cases have dot aligned with line cells. Demo1: dot at col6, line row4, repainted cells (4,6),(4,9),(4,16) = dot columns only?! Earlier: row4 diff cells: (6,6),(9,6),(16,6) only — NOT whole line. So demo1 does NOT recolor whole line; only dot-aligned cells. Demo2 DOES recolor whole line row9. Difference: demo2 has one dot; demo1 three. Hmm.

Wait, maybe demo2 output line row9: "999333" — cols2-5 are 9 while input was 9... Input row9 = 999999 all 9s! So output changed nothing on cols 2-5 (still 9), changed col0 9→9? Input col0 row9 = 9, output col0 = 9 — same! Let me recheck: output row9 = 9 9 9 3 3 3. Col0: input 9 → output 9 (no change). Col3-5: 9→3 (reverted to bg!). So actually: line cells between/after dot got erased, not repainted! Interesting: dot at (2,1); line row9. On line: cell col1 = dot's column → kept as dot color? No, dot color is 0 and line cell is 9... output (9,1)=0, i.e., the dot color replaces the line under the dot's column. Cells col0 and 2 remain 9? col0=9 yes, col2-5 reverted to 3 (bg). Hmm asymmetric.

Compare demo1 line row4: painted cells = dot columns only, dot colors 6 retained. Other line cells stay 9. Consistent: only the dot column of the line gets recolored to dot color. Demo2 col0: why 9 not 3? Because ray from dot passed through line? In demo1 ray stops at line (doesn't reach edge). Demo2: dot row2, line row9, ray down reaches edge row9: passes through line. Col0 on line stays 9 though — that's the far side from the ray direction.

Reconcile: ray travels from dot toward line until it exits grid or hits a line; wherever it crosses a line, it paints the line's cells along... hmm demo2 crosses line9 at col1: paints (9,1)=0. Col0=9 remains 9. Cols 3-5 revert to bg — why? They're part of line; ray doesn't touch them. So output row9 = [9,0,9,9,9,9]? Output shows 9,0,9,9,9,9. Input 9,9,9,9,9,9. So col0: 9→9 unchanged, col1 9→0, cols2-5 9→3?? Wait input row9 is "999999" all 9s and output "909999": positions 2-5 changed 9→9? No — output chars: index0=9,1=0,2=9,3=9,4=9,5=9. Input all 9. So OUTPUT == INPUT on row9 except col1! I misread. OK so line unchanged in demo2. Then output differences in demo2: rows3-8 col1 = 0 (vertical ray from dot down to edge), and nothing else. ✓ Clean.

Demo1 output diffs: vertical rays from each dot UP to line4: dot6: rows3,4(col6 painted 9-line),5,6 → rows3-6 col6 ✓ (painted rows3,4?,5,6: row4 (4,6) is in diff list, color9? Actually (4,6) input 9 stays 9). dot7: rows3-7 col9 ✓ (rows3,4,5,6 dot,row7 dot kept... painted diff (4,9),(5,9)). dot8: rows3-8 col16: diffs (4,16),(5,16),(6,16),(7,16),(8,16)=dot) ✓.
Horizontal bars rows 3&5 (line4±1) spanning per-cluster: {6,9}→5..10 ✓, {16}→15..17 ✓ (anchor minC-1, end maxC+1, clipped).

So full rule: 
- Find full lines (constant color ≠ bg).
- Each dot shoots a ray perpendicular to the NEAREST line, in the direction toward it, painting bg cells until exiting grid or hitting another line, retaining dot positions; cells crossed on a line get the dot's color.
- Additionally horizontal bars on rows line±1 for each line?? Demo1: line1 (row1) has no bar despite being a line. Hmm. Bars only appear for lines near dots? Line1 has no dots. Test has one line with dots both sides: bars rows 9 and 11.

Clustering for bars: demo shows {6,9} cluster (dist 3) → single bar [5,10] (=min-1..max+1). {16} isolated → [15,17] (=15..17, max+1=17). Isolated dot bar = [c-1, c+1] ✓. So clustered: [minC-1, maxC+1]. Threshold 3? With 4 dots below line in test: cols 0,7,11,13. Distances: 7-0=7, 11-7=4, 13-11=2. Cluster {11,13} → bar [10,14]. Single bars {0}:[-1,1]→[0,1], {7}:[6,8]. Plus vertical rays from each dot toward line: dot rows 8 (col5,15), 12 (col0), 14 (col13), 19 (col7,11). From dot to line row10: dot(8,5): ray rows9 (and beyond if passes) — ray stops at line row10, painting row9 col5. Does it pass through? In demo1 rays stopped at the line without continuing (grid edge beyond). Here line10 not edge (row24 is edge). Following demo1 behavior: ray stops at the line. Rows painted between dot and line exclusive of dot: row9 for dots at row8, rows 11..? no wait dots below line: ray goes UP to line row10: dot(12,0): rows 11 only. dot(14,13): row13. dot(19,7): rows 11..13. dot(19,11): rows 11..13.

Do rays stop at line or cross? Demo1 stopped (row2 not painted). Test follows demo1. Good.

Bar rows: line row10 ±1 = rows 9 and 11. Bars from clusters on both rows. Also, do dots ABOVE line paint bars — yes by symmetry, bars depend only on lines, not dot position.

Also check rays for dots at row8 (cols5,15): they're above line; ray downward rows 9 only. But row9 will also contain bars from clusters. Fine, painting order: bars first, rays second (rays overwrite? no conflicts except where ray lands on a bar cell: dot(8,5) ray paints (9,5); bars at rows 9/11. Do rays from dots at row8 also paint on row11? No, stops at line.

Wait, do rays from dots below the line extend beyond line? Demo1 said no. Trust.

Now compute test output manually via code, verify against demo1 with this exact rule (including ray-pass-through variant and bar variants) to pin down. Let me code it:

Rule candidate R1:
- bg=5 (or dominant). Lines: full rows/cols of constant non-bg color.
- dots: non-bg cells not on lines.
- For each dot: direction toward nearest line (Manhattan: sign of row difference or col diff — if line is horizontal, ray vertical toward it).
- Ray: walk from dot toward line, stepping; paint bg cells with dot color; stop before entering line cell? In demo1, dot(6,6) ray up: rows5,4; row4 is the line cell — painted (4,6) became 9 (from 9? no input (4,6)=9 stays 9 — diff showed (4,6) changed 9→9? It was in diff list with value... out diff cells listed earlier had values; (4,6): input 9, output 9? It was in the list [(4,6)...] meaning changed — from 9 to 9? No, diff only lists unequal cells. Input (4,6)=9, output (4,6)=9 — equal! Listed because O[i][j]!=I[i][j]... earlier diff list included (4,6). Contradiction? Earlier diff list: [(3,5),(3,6),...,(4,6),(4,9),(4,16),(5,5)...]. Input row4 = all 9. Output row4 = 9s with 6s kept. So (4,6) input 9 = output 9 — not in diff. The earlier printed diffs included (4,6)? List shows (4, 6) yes... hmm but values equal. Whatever—my manual: ray paints bg cells; line cells never change except under dot column getting dot color? Demo1 row4 col6: input 9, output 9. Demo2 row9 col1: input 9, output 0 (dot color!). So line cell under dot's column DOES change to dot color. Demo1 row4 col6 didn't change... input (4,6)=9, dot color 6 → would become 6. But output (4,6)=9! Contradiction with demo2.

Ugh. Recheck demo2 row9 col1: input row9 = "999999", dot at (2,1) color 0. Output row9 = "909999": col1=0. So dot-colored. Demo1: dots at (6,6),(7,9),(8,16) color 6; line row4; output row4 = "999999699699999969": col6=6, col9=6, col16=6. BOTH show dot color on the line under dot column. My earlier reading of demo1 output row4: "999999699699999969" yes cols 6,9,16 = 6. And diff list included (4,6) because input... input row4 is all 9s; 6≠9 so it IS a diff. OK consistent: ray continues INTO the line and paints line cells, continuing to edge (demo1: line1 at row1, ray from dot(6,6) up passes rows5,4,3,2,1,...,0? Should paint rows2,1,0 col6. But output rows0,2 col6 = 5! Contradiction.)

Demo1 vs Demo2 differ in ray extent... unless demo1 rays don't cross line1 because there's a barrier? OR maybe rays travel only until the grid EDGE in demo2 because the line is at the edge, and in demo1 rays stop at FIRST line. Both are "ray until edge, but lines block". Demo2: line9 is the LAST row; ray from dot(2,1) down: rows3..8 painted, crosses line9, continues off-grid → nothing more. Consistent! Demo1: dot(6,6) up: rows5,4 painted... rows 3,2? Row2,1: row2 not painted (it's bg, between lines), row1 is line. If ray continued past line4 it would hit line1 at row1 and stop (lines block) without painting rows2,0. ✓✓ All consistent!

So ray: move toward nearest line; paint bg cells with dot color; upon entering a line, paint its cell dot-color and STOP (line absorbs). Verify demo1 dot(6,6): steps: (5,6)bg→6? output (5,6)=9... dot color is 6, but output painted cells are 9! Output row5: "555559999995555999" cols5-10 = 9, not 6. Hmm! So painted rays are COLOR 9, the LINE color, not dot color. Dot keeps its color 6. Confusing but consistent: rays paint in line's color.

Recheck demo2: dot(2,1) color 0, line color 9, ray down rows3-8 painted 0! Output rows3-8 col1 = 0. And demo1 painted = 9 (line color). Contradiction: ray color differs per demo... unless ray color = dot color in demo2 and line color in demo1? Inconsistent.

Alternative: rays paint in the color of the object they ORIGINATE... no.

Hmm wait demo2 output row9 col1 = 0: ray from dot passes through line9? If ray stops at line, (9,1) wouldn't be painted. So demo2 ray crosses the line. And demo1 rays... dot(6,6) up: crosses line4? Then rows3,2 painted col6: row3 ✓ painted, row2 ✗ not. UNLESS ray color rules: paint in dot's color until hitting line, then continue painting in line's color. Demo2: dot(2,1): rows3-8 = 0 (dot color) ✓, line row9: cross... continues off-grid, no more cells. But (9,1)=0 painted — dot's color, not line's. If crossing switches to line color, (9,1) should be 9. Unless ray stops AFTER painting line cell in... demo2 (9,1)=0: maybe ray painted dot-color through line too? Then demo1 row3 col6 would be 6, not 9.

Contradiction stands. Difference: demo1 line color 9, demo2 line color 9 too! Dot colors: 6 vs 0. Painted rays: 9 vs 0. So ray color ALWAYS equals LINE color... except demo2 (9,1)=0 and rows3-8=0 which is the DOT color (0≠9). And demo1 rows3-8ish painted 9 = line color.

OH WAIT. Recheck demo2 output row3: "303333" col1=0. Line color 9, dot color 0. Painted 0 = dot color. Demo1 painted 9 = line color?? Dot color 6, line 9. Hmm.

Alternative framing: maybe the painted structure isn't rays but "shadows": In demo1, painted 9-cells = regions shadowed by... The painted areas form rectangles rows3&5 cols5-10 etc. — those ARE bars on rows line±1 (as established). And verticals rows3-6/7/8 col6/9/16: these are the bars' vertical extensions?? Actually reconsider: maybe EVERYTHING is explained as: bars on rows line±1 spanning [minC-1, maxC+1] per cluster, PLUS vertical strips from line to dot edges. Demo2: line row9, dot col1: vertical strip rows1..8 col1? Painted rows3-8 only (rows0,1,2 not painted) — strip only BETWEEN line and dot, not to grid edge. And no horizontal bars in demo2? Rows 8 and 10: row8 = "999333" cols0-2 painted 9; row10 doesn't exist. Horizontal bar on row8 (line-1) spans [0,2] = [c-1, c+1] ✓ single dot cluster! Great, demo2 fits bars too.

So unified: lines attract. Bars on rows line±1, per dot-cluster (dots grouped by proximity, cluster bar = [minC-1, maxC+1] clipped). Vertical strips: between line and farthest dot in each column: from line+1 (or -1) down/up to max dot row, painted dot... demo1 strip col6: rows3-6, but row4 is line; painted rows3,5,6 = dot color 6? Output col6: rows3=9,4=9(line),5=9? row5 col6: "55555999999..." col6=9! Dot color 6 but painted 9. Hmm demo1 strips are 9.

Argh, demo1 strips are 9 and demo2 strips are 0. What distinguishes? Demo1: dot count 3, demo2: 1 dot. Multi-dot vs single dot? Or: strip painted in line color when multiple dots (bars merge conceptually), dot color otherwise? That's ad hoc.

Alternative: maybe in demo1 the "strips" aren't strips—they're ALSO part of bar-logic: rows 3&5 painted because bars exist there. Col6 painted rows 3,5 (bars) and rows 4,6 (dot column through line and dot). So col6 painted set = bar rows + dot column ∩ between line and dot. Col9: bars rows3,5 + dot col rows 3-8 (dot at 7, strip rows3-7 incl line 4)? Output col9: rows3,4,5,6(dot),7 = 9,9,9,6,6 ✓ (strip from line up to dot: rows3,4(line-painted?),5,6,7). Line cell (4,9) painted 6 ✓ (dot color overrides). Col16: strip rows 3-8 (dot at 8): rows3,4,5,6,7,8(dot) ✓ all painted.

Demo2 col1: strip between line(row9) and dot(row2): rows 3..8 ✓ painted 0(dot color). Line cell (9,1)=0 ✓. Bar row8: cols0-2 painted 9 (line color).

So rule for strip: paint dot color from line up to dot (inclusive of line cell under dot). Paint line color on OTHER line cells. Strip color = dot color always. Demo1 col6 strip rows3,5,6: rows 3,5 painted 9?? But they're bar cells (rows line±1)! Bars paint line color. Strips paint dot color. Row5 col6: both bar (row 4+1) and strip → dot wins? But output is 9, not 6. ✗.

Conflict. Unless strips only extend from line to the dot WITHOUT skipping... whatever—maybe simply: final picture = for each dot, draw: vertical segment connecting dot to line (dot color, including line cell under dot if on path) PLUS horizontal bars on line±1 in line color, bars cluster [min-1,max+1]. Demo1 col6 row3,5: bar line color 9 ✓. Demo2 col1 rows3-8: strip = dot color 0 ✓; bar row8 = line color 9 ✓. Conflict zone: cells that are both bar and strip. Demo1 row5 col6: strip says 6, bar says 9 → output 9 → bar wins / or strip doesn't cover it. Demo2 row8 col1: bar says 9, strip (rows3-8 incl 8) says 0 → output 0 → strip wins?! Opposite precedence. Grr.

Unless demo2's rows3-8 col1 isn't a strip but something else... it must be since output has exactly those. And demo1 col6 rows3,5 = 9 coincides with bars. Precedence flips based on whether the dot's ray "arrives"? 

New idea: maybe color = the color you move ALONG rows... no. Simplest workable model: ray from dot toward line, painting dot color everywhere (bg cells and line cells), BUT in demo1 we see 9 not 6. Re-examine demo1 raw output row3: "555559999995555999". And input row3 all 5. Painted cols5-10,15-17 = 9. Dot colors ALL 6 in demo1. So bars are 9=line color, confirmed. Demo2 bar row8 = 9 = line color, confirmed. Demos consistent on bars.

Strips: demo1 cols6,9,16 rows between line and dots = line color 9. Demo2 col1 rows3-8 = dot color 0. Difference between demos: demo1 strips are between line AND dots where the bar logic already covers rows 3,5... col6: strip rows 3,4,5,6; bar covers rows 3,5; strip adds nothing visible (rows4,6: row4 line cell→dot color6 ✓; row6 dot kept). Demo2: strip adds rows3-7 (row8 bar). Row8 col1 = 0: strip wins over bar. Hmm but maybe in demo2 the bar is [c-1,c+1]=[0,2] painted 9 — row8 col1 is inside. Strip color 0.

Difference: maybe strip color = line color in demo1 because... line and dot colors swapped roles? Demo1: bg 5, line 9, dot 6. Demo2: bg 3, line 9, dot 0. Painted strip colors: 9, 0. = line, dot. Is there any global invariant? Maybe: painted ray color = the NON-dominant... or maybe the rule is: every drawn element takes the color of the LATEST/nearest "source": bars emanate from lines (line color), strips emanate from dots (dot color), and conflict resolution favors the source closer to... demo1 row5: closer to line(row4)? distance1 vs dot(6) distance1 tie. Demo2 row8: closer to line(9,dist1) than dot(2,dist6) yet dot wins. Distance-to-source along column: demo2 row8: sources line(d=1), dot(d=6) → line closer → line color expected, got dot. So not distance.
